long_biography.plain_text:
Trained in economics and law, Víctor Urrutia Vallejo inherited links to two long-standing Spanish industrial families. His paternal forebears helped build energy businesses that fed into Iberdrola, while his maternal family founded CVNE. He joined Iberdrola’s board in his thirties and later became vice-chairman, then directed the family’s investments through Asúa Inversiones.

Urrutia became CVNE president in 2004 and held the office for more than two decades as the family vehicle consolidated control of the winery and diversified across listed companies. A formal succession followed in 2025–26: his son Víctor Juan assumed the CVNE chair, and Juan Ramón became president of Asúa. Urrutia remains Asúa’s beneficial owner and invests through its portfolio.
